builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Latency and accuracy tradeoffs in Spiking Neural Networks
summary: Falcon replaces the assumption that SNN latency scales with local timesteps by overlapping computation across layers at the timestep level, then selecting per-layer pipeline delays and tuning firing thresholds and initial membrane potentials via spike-based quantization-aware training. The cost is a full retraining and per-layer search pipeline plus dependence on a spatial analog compute-in-memory substrate with shared digital engines, which the reader does not possess. The method can fail because spikes fired on incomplete inputs cannot be withdrawn, so aggressive overlap permanently degrades accuracy, and the paper shows added waiting can itself make the network both slower and less accurate at certain layers.
rationale: The technique targets spiking neural networks on analog compute-in-memory neuromorphic hardware, which is outside the reader's GPU/API production stack and offers no transferable gain for standard LLM or ML workloads.

claims.statement: Falcon replaces the assumption that SNN latency scales with local timesteps by overlapping computation across layers at the timestep level, then selecting per-layer pipeline delays and tuning firing thresholds and initial membrane potentials via spike-based quantization-aware training. The cost is a full retraining and per-layer search pipeline plus dependence on a spatial analog compute-in-memory substrate with shared digital engines, which the reader does not possess. The method can fail because spikes fired on incomplete inputs cannot be withdrawn, so aggressive overlap permanently degrades accuracy, and the paper shows added waiting can itself make the network both slower and less accurate at certain layers.

Achieves 96.31% (GSCV2) and 83.02% (SSC) accuracy at modeled network-core latencies of 119.64us and 124.00us respectively under a spatial analog compute-in-memory mapping; no multiplicative speedup factor over a stated baseline is given.
